At the SEMA Show next month, active safety engineers from General Motors and Ford will provide a look behind the engineering decisions that influence vehicle safety before, during, and after a collision.

They’ll speak during the second session of the Society of Collision Repair Specialists’ (SCRS) 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit, titled “ Engineering the Safety Benefit: From Requirements to Real-World Performance ,” Thursday, Nov. 5, from 2–3 p.m.

It will follow an earlier session featuring National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) Deputy Administrator Lee White from 12:30–1:30 p.m. White will examine vehicle safety priorities and the agency’s role in advancing safety on U.S. roadways.

To register for all three OEM Summit sessions, visit here .

An SCRS RDE Full Series Pass provides access to Tuesday and Wednesday RDE sessions, the IDEAS Collide Showcase, Thursday’s OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit, and the SCRS Afterparty.

Register for the full series pass here .

“This second session will move from those broader safety objectives into the vehicle itself, examining how automakers translate requirements and safety goals into technologies designed to produce measurable real-world benefits,” an SCRS press release states. “The afternoon will then progress to the collision repair environment, exploring how those engineered capabilities are preserved and restored after a vehicle has been damaged.”

The second session will bring together engineers who are responsible for developing, evaluating, and measuring advanced vehicle safety systems. Attendees will learn about the engineering decisions that influence vehicle safety.

Panelists include Michael Carpenter, General Motors Active Safety and Global Vehicle Performance owner; Jameson Collins, General Motors Active Safety and staff product manager; and Jeremy Nelson, Ford Motor Co. ADAS application systems engineer.

Carpenter works within GM Global Product Safety, Systems, and Certification on ADAS technology and performance strategies, new technology development, implementation of regulatory and consumer metric requirements, ADAS field effectiveness and safety benefits, and industry collaboration on standards and test-method development.

Collins leads product strategy, roadmap development, and delivery for GM’s Active Safety features, translating customer needs, competitive insights, and regulatory requirements into technologies intended to improve safety and the driving experience.

Nelson focuses on the development, release, integration, and servicing of advanced driver assistance system domain controllers. He supports vehicle production and development milestones while troubleshooting ADAS components and working across engineering, quality, and product development teams to ensure systems perform safely and as intended.

The discussion will be moderated by Jake Rodenroth, automotive industry executive, and will move beyond what ADAS features do to examine why they exist, how their intended performance is established, and how their effectiveness is evaluated. This will include what it means when a safety system is absent, disabled, damaged, or operating outside its intended parameters.

The release states: “That progression leads directly to a fundamental question for collision repair professionals: If a vehicle entered a collision with a measurable safety capability, how can the repairer know that capability has been restored?”

The panel will also explore ADAS feature development, real-world effectiveness, crash avoidance and mitigation, implications of inoperable systems, verification of safety performance, and the potential for system degradation.

The 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit is part of SCRS’ Repairer Driven Education (RDE) program at the SEMA Show.

“The Summit brings collision repair professionals together with automakers, engineers, regulators, and other subject-matter experts to examine emerging technologies and their implications for safe and complete vehicle repair,” the release states.

During the first session, White will present on the agency’s current vehicle and roadway safety priorities, emerging transportation technologies, data-driven research, and the federal government’s work with the industry to reduce fatalities and serious injuries, an SCRS release states.

Following White’s presentation, he will sit down with Aaron Schulenburg, SCRS executive director, for a one-on-one conversation exploring the intersection between federal safety objectives, automotive innovation, and the collision repair industry’s role in preserving vehicle safety throughout its service life.

NHTSA sits at the center of many discussions that impact the collision repair industry.

During a July Collision Industry Conference meeting, Schulenburg discussed NHTSA’s investigation into counterfeit airbag s with Teena Bohi, an Automotive Anti-Counterfeiting Council (A2C2) Board member.

In April, NHTSA announced a ban on one type of counterfeit airbag part . Before the ban, it also issued an “urgent” industry alert specifically asking the auto repair industry to look for dangerous airbag inflators.

Repair procedures are impacted by NHTSA-mandated vehicle safety technology. This includes mandated backup cameras in all new vehicles under 10,000 pounds as of May 2018.

NHTSA also has a final rule that mandates automatic emergency braking (AEB) in pedestrian vehicles by September 2029.

However, NHTSA also announced it paused the rule to give the Trump administration time to review it following pushback and a lawsuit filed by the Alliance of Automotive Innovation (Auto Innovators) .

The 2004-2013 Mazda 3 is based on the Ford global C1 platform, shared with the European Ford Focus and Volvo S40. Nothing is really groundbreaking about the mechanical brake system, but not paying attention to the details can end in a post-brake-job comeback.

A key service issue concerns the hydraulics and ABS system. The older the car, the greater the chance the brake fluid has not been serviced. Over time this can cause issues with the ABS hydraulic control unit.

For almost 10 years, Mazda used the same caliper, pad and rotor design. Pads should be replaced when there is 2mm or less of friction material. If the rotors are any thicker, they have enough material on them to last at least one turning on the lathe. The runout specification for these vehicles is .002” and disc thickness variation should be far below .0005”.

Mazda claims repeated panic braking may raise the temperature in some portions of the disc plate by approx. 1,000°C (l,832°F). This temperature is almost near impossible to achieve this side of a high-speed police chase.

The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 75 ft./lbs.

All Mazda3 models have rear disc brakes. The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 55 ft./lbs.

Mazda uses a hand brake that is incorporated into the rear caliper, and a couple of systems are employed to retract rear pistons. The later-model cars require the familiar method of turning the piston clockwise while applying pressure, where others will have a plug on the back side of the caliper that provides access for an Allen wrench to facilitate retracting the piston. Be careful as you retract the piston.

After the pads are replaced, pump the pedal and adjust the parking brake mechanism in the rear calipers. If the level has too much travel, perform the following steps:

Remove the service hole cover of the rear console.

Turn the adjusting nut and adjust the parking brake lever.

After adjustment, pull the parking brake lever one notch and verify that the parking brake warning light illuminates and the rear brakes do not drag.

The Mazda3 comes in two styles, ABS and ABS with Dynamic Stability Control (DSC). Both systems connect to other vehicle components via a high-speed serial data bus. The DSC system ties more components together (like a yaw/pitch sensor and steering position sensor) onto the bus.

If you are seeing communication-related DTCs, it is essential that you fully diagnose problems with the system before you start replacing sensors and modules. Some of these vehicles have been on the road for more than six years and the connections will be starting to corrode and fret.

One of the main facilitators of ABS/DCS problems are the connectors, especially under the hood where the control/modulator unit connects. Being able to measure values at the connectors and observe data on a scan tool is essential for diagnosing problems.

The biggest ABS issue with the three generations of Mazda 3 is power. With some higher mileage vehicles, the battery cables, wiring from the power distribution box or the ground connection (behind the driver’s side headlight at G02) can have enough resistance so the voltage drops below 8 volts. When this happens, the ABS module cuts control and the electronic brake distribution system is disabled.

If a modulator/control unit is replaced, the pressure sensors must be recalibrated with a scan tool that is able to communicate with the chassis/ABS module. If this is not performed, it can result in brake failure and lock up.

If you have DTCs C1141, C1142, C1143, C1144, C1233, C1234, C1235 or C1236 (ABS wheel-speed sensor/ABS sensor rotor), chances are something is wrong with the wheel bearings. Another cause for these codes could be an accumulation of metal debris on the sensor. The front bearings are press-in cartridge-style units. Rear wheel bearings are hub units. In the front, the tone ring, or encoder, is on the inner seal of the bearing and the sensor is mounted in the knuckle. The parameters for these codes to be set include abnormalities in the signal such as a weak signal or large differences in the value when compared to the other sensors.

If you have DTCs C1145, C1155, C1165 or C1175 (open sensor), it could be damaged wiring or a failed sensor that is the problem. If you have more than one, chances are there is a problem with the connection at the control unit or in the front or rear harnesses of the sensors.

These DTCs will usually clear themselves after repairs are made and the vehicle is driven above 6.2 mph when the self-diagnostic check is performed.

Some customers may report a slight clunk, bang or jolt from the front of the vehicle. This concern will most likely occur during the vehicle’s first forward movement and after the vehicle sits for a few hours and/or a cold soak. This is a normal operating noise of the ABS system.

If you encounter a customer complaint for this concern, explain that the noise comes from the ABS/TCS/DSC “Malfunction Detection Function” initial check. The initial check is a necessary function to ensure the normal operation of the ABS/TCS/DSC system. The timing of the presentation put that support into action immediately. Later Tuesday, members of the MBHS Auto Club Kart Racing Team were scheduled to travel to K1 Speed in Clovis to compete in Round 10 of the Teen Challenge GP.

The presentation was attended by Dr. Eric Prater, SLCUSD Superintendent; Dan Neff, SLCUSD Secondary Director; and Michael Franklin, MBHS Principal, along with students and community supporters.

The MBHS Automotive Program combines classroom instruction, hands-on shop experience, competition and career-connected learning. Through the ASB Auto Club, students also participate in kart racing, automotive events and other activities that provide opportunities to develop teamwork and professional skills beyond the classroom.

For Wimmer, the donation also demonstrates to students that Morro Bay’s automotive community is invested in their future.

“When students see organizations like the Cruisin’ Morro Bay Car Show supporting them, they see that the community values what they’re working toward,” Wimmer said. “Whether they’re representing MBHS at a competition or heading to Cuesta College to continue their automotive education, we want them to know there are people behind them.”

Morro Bay High School and the MBHS Automotive Program thank Vesterfelt and the Cruisin’ Morro Bay Car Show, including its organizers, volunteers, participants and sponsors, for their continued investment in local students.

Imagine being a belt on the front of the engine. Yours is a balancing act that is always being upset by change from the inputs from the crank pulley and the loads from the alternator, AC compressor and maybe a power steering pump. Your mission is to keep in contact with the grooves on the pulleys. You can’t hold on too tightly, because it could decrease fuel economy and damage the bearings inside the water pump, idler bushings and other components. But you can’t be too loose because it will cause you to slip, resulting in wear and noise.

- What Sets a Slow-Response O2 or Air/Fuel Sensor Code?

- Six Tips for Building and Selling a Better Timing Belt Job

- How Modules Manage Electrical and Mechanical Loads

A serpentine belt transfers torque through friction between its ribs and the pulley grooves. The belt must be held tightly enough against the pulleys to prevent slipping under the system’s maximum expected expected load.

As mentioned before, if tension is too low, the belt can microslip or visibly slip. This generates heat, polishes the belt ribs and pulley grooves, and may produce a chirp or squeal. Slippage can also reduce alternator output, power steering assist, coolant-pump speed or AC compressor performance.

Excessive tension creates a different set of problems. Every accessory shaft experiences a radial load from the belt. Raising belt tension increases that load, which can accelerate bearing wear in the alternator, water pump, idlers, tensioner and AC compressor. It also increases belt fatigue as the belt repeatedly bends around the pulleys. The additional bearing friction and belt deformation represent a small but measurable parasitic loss.

The correct tension is consequently the lowest tension that can reliably transmit the required torque under all operating conditions. That reduces friction and improves efficiency while preserving traction and controlling noise.

An automatic tensioner’s spring applies the required static tension, while an internal damping mechanism controls rapid arm movement. The damping prevents the tensioner from bouncing in response to engine firing pulses and accessory-load changes. Insufficient tension causes slippage, heat and noise, while excessive tension contributes to accessory wear. Some belt companies tensioner guidance also identifies excessive arm oscillation as a sign of a failed damping system or another drive-system problem.

What Happens When Accessory Load Increases?

The belt does not have identical tension everywhere around its path. When the crankshaft is driving an accessory, the belt span pulling the accessory pulley becomes the tight side. The belt leaving that pulley has less tension. The difference between those forces, combined with pulley radius, produces the torque that turns the accessory.

When alternator electrical output increases, electromagnetic resistance inside the alternator rises. The crankshaft must supply more torque through the belt. The tension difference across the alternator pulley increases, and the belt may elongate elastically by a very small amount. The tensioner moves to manage that change.

A hydraulic power steering pump produces a similar reaction when the driver turns the steering wheel, especially near the steering stop. Pump pressure and required input torque rise rapidly. On systems with belt-driven AC compressors, compressor engagement can create an even sharper load change.

These loads are why a belt drive may operate quietly in the bay but squeal when the headlights, blower motor and rear defroster are switched on, when the steering wheel is turned at idle or when the AC compressor engages. The added load exposes marginal tension, worn ribs, pulley contamination or misalignment.

Technicians should reproduce the operating condition instead of judging the drive only at unloaded idle.

Engine-Speed Changes and Tension Reversals

Crankshaft speed is not perfectly constant. Each combustion event accelerates the crankshaft, while compression strokes and drivetrain events slow it. Those variations become more pronounced during startup, shutdown, throttle changes, transmission shifts and cylinder-deactivation transitions.

During acceleration, the belt must accelerate the rotating mass of every accessory. The alternator is particularly important because its rotor normally turns several times faster than the crankshaft. Its inertia resists a sudden increase in belt speed.

During rapid engine deceleration, the situation changes. The alternator rotor wants to continue spinning and can momentarily drive against the decelerating belt. The normal tight- and slack-side relationship does not permanently swap during ordinary operation, because the crankshaft remains the primary power source. However, local belt forces can equalize or briefly reverse during a transient event. The tensioner arm may then move sharply as the tension disturbance travels through the drive.

This can produce intermittent chirps, belt slap or tensioner rattle that does not occur at steady engine speed. A noise heard only during startup, shutdown, throttle tip-in or a downshift is therefore an important diagnostic clue.

Many late-model applications use an overrunning alternator pulley or overrunning alternator decoupler  (OAD) to control these events. The pulley allows the alternator to overrun the belt during rapid deceleration. An OAD also uses an internal torsion spring to absorb speed and tension fluctuations. This arrangement reduces vibration and allows the alternator to freewheel during deceleration.

A seized decoupler can act like a solid pulley, causing excessive tensioner movement and a chirp during startup or shutdown. Installing a solid pulley where an OAD was specified can create noise and shorten belt and tensioner life.

Why Replace the Belt and Tensioner Together?

The newly published EuroBrake 2026 Review captures the key discussions, technical developments and industry perspectives shared at this year’s event in Mainz, Germany.

EuroBrake 2026 brought together more than 1,100 braking industry experts, researchers and engineers from vehicle manufacturers, suppliers, universities and research organisations around the world.

The event examined how braking technology is evolving from a standalone mechanical system into a fully integrated component of next-generation vehicle architecture.

Key areas explored throughout the technical programme included:

Artificial intelligence, software and digital engineering

Non-exhaust emissions and Euro 7 readiness

Electrification and regenerative braking

Standardisation and regulatory developments

Automation, advanced driver assistance systems and future mobility

Cross-industry collaboration across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, rail and motorsport

The review brings together highlights from the keynote presentations, panel discussions, technical sessions and exhibition, providing an overview of the ideas and innovations shaping the future of braking and friction technology.

EuroBrake 2026 was made possible by the contributions of its keynote speakers, panellists, authors, Steering Committee members, sponsors, more than 110 exhibitors and the wider delegate community.

Their combined expertise created an international forum for technical exchange, collaboration and discussion across the global braking industry.

The brake system is no longer just a safety component, but a critical part of a complex, integrated and intelligent vehicle system, writes Michael Nash

If it’s June, it’s EuroBrake, and this year it was the turn of the historic city of Mainz in Germany to once again welcome over 1,100 brake system stakeholders for EuroBrake 2026.

A thriving community of engineers, technical specialists, thought leaders, and researchers gathered on the banks of the River Rhine for a packed three-day programme of keynotes, panel discussions, and technical presentations that delved into the latest innovations and challenges in brake and friction technology.

Disruption through product evolution and trend influence were at the heart of the discussions at the 14 th edition of EuroBrake. Electrification, automation, connectivity and sustainability are reshaping the way vehicles are being designed and used, and the brake is no longer just a safety component but must be considered as part of a complex, integrated and intelligent system.

With an eye on the next generation of brake system engineers, EuroBrake also offers students a unique chance to hear from and connect with potential employers

This system has become increasingly digitalised, and therefore, the influence of software on braking components has grown. AI is pushing this one step further. Leveraging data from in-vehicle sensors enables smarter control and braking functionality, enhancing driving performance and providing customers with refined support capability. AI has also become an integral tool for engineers in the development and optimisation of systems, making the process faster and more efficient.

On the subject of efficiency, the EuroBrake OEM Panel rifled through a selection of topics, touching on some of the key challenges facing the wider automotive industry. Experts from BMW, Volkswagen Group, Stellantis, Audi and NIO all agreed that the industry is on the cusp of huge change with the implementation of brake-by-wire, opening up new possibilities for enhanced stability control and vehicle performance as well as promising avenues for platform design. Regenerative braking and weight reduction through system consolidation will benefit battery EVs, while brand identification through customisable pedal feedback could allow OEMs to connect with customers in a completely new way.

Experts from BMW, Volkswagen Group, Stellantis, Audi and NIO all agreed that the industry is on the cusp of huge change with the implementation of brake-by-wire

Yet, the promise of innovation and the next generation of braking technology does not reduce the importance of optimising and improving existing friction solutions. Material developments and process refinement are consistently resulting in new disc, pad, and rotor designs. Suppliers are identifying new ways of tackling old issues such as wear, corrosion, thermal stress, and inertia, while the introduction of recycled content is no longer having a detrimental impact on performance or durability.

Reducing particulate matter (PM) emissions also remains a critical aspect of brake and friction technology development, particularly in the commercial vehicle (CV) and rail sectors. A comprehensive mix of simulation and real-world field trials shows significant potential for emissions reduction, with several speakers presenting detailed reports on their findings and offering a unique glimpse into their testing processes.

For rail, addressing the impact of high speeds and extreme conditions on friction components is a primary concern, while coping with the change of driving profiles, from urban to highway, poses challenges for brake systems used in the heavy-duty vehicle segment. And although each use-case has its own specifics, the fundamental principles are similar across rail, CV, motorcycle, and passenger car brakes.

Electrification, automation, connectivity and sustainability are reshaping the way vehicles are being designed and used, and the brake is no longer just a safety component but must be considered as part of a complex, integrated and intelligent system

Outside of the auditoriums and presentations, the bustle of the halls and exhibitor stands made it evidently clear that EuroBrake remains a vital networking event for the global braking and friction technology community, giving peers a chance to meet in person, network, and share opinions and ideas.

With a keen eye on the next generation of brake system engineers, EuroBrake also offers students a unique chance to hear from and connect with potential employers. When these budding engineers enter the workforce, they’ll be joining the industry during a period of unparalleled disruption – and with disruption comes opportunity.

Michael Nash is an independent automotive industry writer and FISITA contributor

Carlisle Brake & Friction is one of five [CentroMotion](https://www.centromotion.com/) brands exhibiting at bauma, April 7–13 in Munich,booth A2, 402.

CentroMotion is a global manufacturing company specializing in friction, information and controls, mechanical power transmission, and thermal and motion control products.

_**Our teams will showcase various products that serve the construction market:**_

[Carlise Brake & Friction](https://carlislecbf.com/)
Sharing product highlights from their industry-leading brake, transmissions/clutch and motion control systems.

[CrossControl](https://crosscontrol.com/)
Showcasing display and on-board computing platforms.

[GITS Mfg.](https://www.gitsmfg.com/products/)
Featuring the latest solutions in thermal management solutions, including intake throttle valves, exhaust recirculation valves and exhaust back-pressure valves for diesel, gas, and hydrogen internal combustion engines.

[Maximatecc](https://www.maximatecc.com/)
Demonstrating micro-controller-based platforms for instrumentation and HMI.

[Power-Packer](https://www.power-packer.com/)
Exhibiting new electro-hydraulic actuators with a design focus on efficiency, perfectly suited for power-on-demand functions in mobile applications.

8月22~24日，2026年中国大学生机械工程创新创意大赛“北起院杯”物流技术创意赛全国总决赛在武汉理工大学圆满举行。江西华伍制动器股份有限公司受邀参加本次赛事，公司总经理熊涛担任大赛总决赛裁判，总工程师杜军华在同期举办的全国高校机械物流类专业建设研讨会上作主题分享，以企业力量赋能青年学子创新实践，推动产学研深度融合。

本次大赛由中国机械工程学会主办，作为一项入选《全国普通高校大学生竞赛分析报告》竞赛目录的国家级学科竞赛，旨在“以赛促学、以赛促教、以赛促创”。赛事聚焦物料搬运行业实际应用场景，以“散料货物搬运机器人”为命题方向，要求参赛团队自主研发具备智能识别、自主导航与精准抓取功能的搬运机器人，全面考核机器视觉、路径规划、精密机械控制等关键技术。本届赛事共有81所高校、397支队伍、2400余名师生参与，经过五大赛区层层选拔，最终115项优秀作品晋级总决赛。

熊涛总经理在决赛现场认真观摩参赛作品演示，从工程应用角度对参赛项目进行专业评审。作为大赛总决赛裁判，他以丰富的行业实践经验为参赛学子提供专业指导，激励青年人才勇于创新、敢于突破。

在同期举办的全国高校机械物流类专业建设研讨会上，总工程师杜军华作了《工业制动系统绿色、智能技术的研究和应用》主题分享。他从工业制动系统的技术演进出发，结合华伍在港口、风电、矿山等领域的工程实践，与参会专家深入探讨了制动系统智能化、绿色化的发展方向，以及产教融合对行业人才培养的推动作用。

从担任大赛裁判到参与专业建设研讨，华伍股份正以多元方式深度融入高校科创生态。未来，公司将继续践行产学研协同发展的理念，以产业实践经验助力高校人才培养，为行业创新发展持续注入活力。

作为升船机安全运行的核心保障设备，制动系统与驱动系统紧密配合，共同实现承船厢的正常启动、快速停机及紧急安全制动，其性能可靠性直接关系到升船机整体运行安全。

华伍股份深耕升船机安全制动领域多年，凭借扎实的技术积累与丰富的工程实践经验，承接了向家坝升船机承船厢制动系统自主可控研究与应用项目。项目启动以来，公司围绕机械制动器、液压系统、电控系统三大板块，全面推进关键零部件选型对比、专项试验验证及系统设计研制工作，稳步开展制动系统自主可控技术研究，致力于打造安全可靠、自主可控的升船机制动系统解决方案。

根据项目进展，8月20~21日，向家坝“升船机承船厢制动系统自主可控研究与应用设计联络会”在江西丰城顺利召开。本次会议由三峡金沙江川云水电开发有限公司宜宾向家坝电厂组织，业主单位、特邀行业专家及华伍股份项目团队共同参会。

会议期间，业主单位代表赴试验室现场，见证了制动系统机械、液压和电气部分的试验项目。随后，华伍股份项目团队围绕制动系统机械、液压、电气三部分的设计图纸及试验报告等技术文件进行了详细汇报。与会人员认真听取汇报，并就关键技术细节展开深入讨论，华伍股份项目团队对专家提出的问题逐一作出详尽解答。经充分研讨，专家组一致认为项目已完成机械、液压、电气三部分自主可控研究工作，研究内容满足合同要求，同意华伍股份依据选型结果及设计图纸推进下一阶段工作。

向家坝水电站是金沙江下游梯级开发中的最后一个梯级，其升船机承船厢制动系统原全套设备由国外公司集成供货，核心部件长期依赖进口，存在供应链风险高、运维响应慢、核心技术不可控等突出问题。本项目旨在研究制动系统从机械执行机构、液压系统到电气控制系统的全过程自主可控替代，对于打破技术依赖、保障国家重大水利基础设施安全稳定运行具有重要意义。

此次设计联络会的顺利召开，标志着项目自主可控研究工作取得阶段性重要成果，为后续设备生产、系统联调及现场应用奠定了坚实基础。华伍股份将继续发挥在升船机制动领域的技术优势，以严谨的工程态度和扎实的研发实力，高质量推进项目各项工作，为我国水利装备自主可控贡献华伍力量。

8月12日，三一传动事业部首届电驱动供应商大会在江苏苏州隆重召开。华伍股份作为核心供应商应邀参会，公司总经理熊涛、副总经理王志成、总经理助理王国林出席大会。熊涛总经理代表公司与三一传动签署战略合作协议，标志着双方合作迈入全面深化新阶段。

本次大会以“质领电驱 共筑未来”为主题，汇聚了全国各地40余家优质配套厂商。会议期间，三一传动发布了五年战略目标，明确提出从传统制造向汽车级零部件标准转型的硬性要求，强调供应商须从传统的“合格率”思维转向PPM级别的质量管控标准，并号召合作伙伴加大研发与人才投入，共建具有全球竞争力的供应链体系。

会上举行了隆重的签约仪式，华伍股份与三一传动正式建立电驱动领域长期战略合作关系。未来，双方将围绕新能源工程设备赛道，在产品研发、质量管控、交付保障等方面开展更深层次协同。华伍股份将与三一传动共同应对行业电动化浪潮，从产品供应转向技术协同与价值共创，携手推动新能源工程机械产业高质量发展。

会议期间，三一集团董事、三一重工总裁俞宏福作闭幕总结。他指出，三一传动旨在解决中国传动系统薄弱环节的行业痛点，呼吁合作伙伴亲自下场狠抓质量，要求供应商企业一把手必须亲临现场解决实际问题，不能仅停留在口头承诺。会议还发布了三一传动的战略愿景、质量策划及供应链协同规划，为与会供应商指明了合作方向。

此次战略协议的签署，是华伍股份深耕高端装备制动系统领域的重要里程碑。作为行业领先的制动系统解决方案提供商，华伍股份将以此为契机，全面对标三一传动战略目标和PPM级质量标准，依托自身在制动系统领域的技术积累与制造优势，进一步提升产品一致性与交付保障能力，深度融入三一传动电驱动供应链协同体系。公司将与三一携手，共同迎接新能源工程机械行业机遇，助力中国高端装备制造走向世界。

盛夏七月，备受关注的“一带一路”中非合作重点工程——阿尔及利亚Tosyali 1780mm酸洗-冷连轧项目圆满完成热试。作为北非首条酸洗冷轧高端产线，该项目成功填补了北非地区高端冷轧钢材生产的市场空白，标志着北非钢铁产业迈向高端智能化新阶段。作为国内工业制动领域龙头企业，华伍股份深度参与本次项目，为工程全套供应191台气动盘式制动器，以可靠的国产制动技术，为产线安全、高效、稳定运行筑牢核心安全屏障。

该项目由中钢国际EPC总包承建，坐拥先进的生产工艺流程、一流的核心设备配置，搭载全线智能控制系统，同时兼顾绿色环保生产标准，是北非地区智能化、绿色化钢铁制造的标杆项目。冶金冷轧生产线工况复杂、连续作业强度大，对配套制动设备的稳定性、散热性、适配性有着极为严苛的行业要求，核心制动设备的性能直接关乎整条产线的生产安全与运行效率。

针对本次项目严苛的冶金工况，华伍股份配套的气动盘式制动器，凭借制动平稳、响应迅速、散热高效、耐用性强的核心优势，完美适配冷轧产线连续化、智能化生产需求，有效规避高速轧制过程中的设备滑移、制动失灵等安全隐患，全方位保障产线设备启停精准、运行可控，充分印证了国产工业制动装备的硬核品质。 此次顺利配套交付并成功助力项目热试，是华伍股份深耕海外冶金工程市场的重要标志性成果。作为工业制动领域民族企业，华伍股份始终坚持技术创新，持续打磨产品性能，凭借成熟稳定的制动解决方案、过硬的产品质量和完善的服务体系，深耕“一带一路”海外市场。

未来，华伍股份将持续发力海外高端装备配套领域，以优质国产智造赋能全球工业升级，持续拓展中非、中阿产业合作版图，让国产制动技术与装备走向更多海外市场，助力共建“一带一路”高质量发展。

7月21日，中国重型机械工业协会专家组一行走进华伍股份开展专精特新企业专项调研。调研组由协会常务副理事长景晓波带队，唐超、王继生、王淼、王建梅校长、李国杰教授等行业权威专家莅临公司，实地考察智能制造产线、综合实验室，并与公司管理层、技术骨干座谈交流，深度把脉企业细分赛道创新发展之路。公司总经理熊涛及核心管理、技术团队全程陪同调研。

专家组先后参观多功能展厅、综合实验室，现场观摩多系列核心制动产品生产线，详细询问公司技术攻关、国产替代、数字化转型等落地成果。深耕工业制动领域三十余载的华伍股份，成长路径清晰扎实：企业创立之初，聚焦起重机械制动配件生产，打破国外品牌在国内港口制动市场的垄断；2010年成功登陆深交所，成为国内制动行业首家上市企业；多年来持续深耕细分赛道，逐步拓展起重运输、港口装卸、风电、水工、矿山等高端装备制动市场，建成国家级博士后工作站、专业制动综合检测实验室，牵头制定多项国家及行业标准，先后获评江西省专精特新企业、细分领域制造业单项冠军，多款自主产品填补国内技术空白，远销全球多国。

座谈会上，总经理熊涛结合企业发展历程，向专家组全面汇报专精特新建设成效、产业布局与发展痛点。他表示，从单一起重制动配件到覆盖多领域高端制动系统研发制造，企业始终坚守主业、坚持自主研发，当前重点布局矿山机械等新兴赛道；同时也结合企业经营实际，反映行业细分零部件企业普遍面临的发展堵点，期盼协会充分发挥桥梁纽带作用，打通主机厂与零部件企业供需渠道，搭建政企常态化沟通机制，为行业细分龙头企业纾困解难、赋能成长。 与会专家充分肯定华伍股份数十年深耕细分赛道、坚持自主创新、推进进口替代的发展模式，对公司高端制动技术研发、数字化智能产线建设成果给予高度评价。景晓波副理事长指出，重型机械产业链自主可控离不开华伍这类专精特新配套龙头，协会将持续收集企业发展诉求，向上反馈行业共性难题，搭建供需对接、标准创新、政策申报三大服务平台，赋能细分零部件企业做强做大。王建梅校长、李国杰教授从产学研协同攻关、极端工况可靠性测试等方面给出专业指导，建议公司依托科研平台持续布局前沿技术，筑牢细分领域技术壁垒。

此次调研为公司高质量发展提供专业指引。华伍股份表示，将认真吸纳专家组意见建议，延续三十余年专注深耕的发展初心，持续走专精特新发展道路，聚焦高端制动装备技术攻关，补齐产业链短板，深化数智化绿色制造升级，发挥行业示范引领作用，携手上下游完善国产重型装备制动供应链，以核心零部件自主创新助力我国重型机械产业高端化、智能化、绿色化发展。

为进一步深化校企协同创新，推动人才链与产业链深度融合，依托双方此前签订的全面合作框架协议及共建人才联合培养实践基地的合作基础，7月12日至17日，华伍股份迎来了武汉理工大学39名学子，开展了为期五天的专项实习实践培训，搭建起高校人才培养与企业产业发展的精准对接桥梁。

武汉理工大学在起重、港口机械领域具备深厚的学科优势，双方具备天然的产业契合度与技术协同基础。本次实训是双方从协议合作走向实质育人、从理论协同走向实践落地的重要举措。公司创新构建了“骨干带教+车间研学+课题实操”的全方位培养模式，助力青年学子知行合一、学以致用。

7月13日，培训开营仪式顺利举行。本次培训搭建了循序渐进的课程体系，内容涵盖企业概况、安全教育、质量体系学习及技术系统课程。学员分组配备专属导师，一对一定向指导实习课题、解答专业难点。理论学习之外，公司组织学员深入铸造、金工、结构、轨交、总装五大核心生产车间参观学习，近距离观摩零部件加工、精密装配、成品检测等全生产流程，将课堂理论与生产实践深度结合，有效补齐了工程实操短板。实训期间，公司还组织了校企青年篮球友谊赛，增进交流互动，同时全方位落实食宿、安全等后勤保障，为学子营造了舒适安心的实训环境。

7月17日，实训圆满结营。各组学员依次完成课题成果汇报，校企双方共同复盘总结实训成效。校方对公司系统化、精细化的实训组织安排给予了高度认可。 此次专项实训有效提升了高校学子的工程实践能力与专业应用水平，也为公司储备优质青年人才搭建了良好平台。下一步，华伍股份将持续深化校企合作，常态化开展实践教学、联合科研、课题攻关与人才输送工作，构建人才共育、技术共研、成果共享的长效合作机制，以高质量人才培育赋能企业技术创新与产业升级。

湿式制动器是公司近年来重点开发的核心安全部件，广泛应用于工程机械与重型车辆传动制动系统。该产品依靠多组弹簧或碟簧提供驻车制动压紧力，制动力矩大、承载工况严苛，对装配一致性及螺纹紧固可靠性有着极高要求。面对订单交付周期紧、装配过程耗时费力的难题，工艺管理部与总装车间协同发力，针对湿式制动器装配难点开展系统性工艺攻关，取得了显著成效。

在湿式制动器装配过程中，需克服强大弹簧力以安装座盖紧固螺栓。以HSPA150250产品为例，其弹簧组多达27组，前期装配需先安装5颗M16螺栓逐步压紧座盖，随着弹簧不断压缩，弹力持续增大，螺栓紧固愈发费力，加之工作台高度仅20至30厘米，作业员需长时间弯腰或下蹲操作，完成这5颗螺栓的紧固耗时约30分钟，严重拖累装配节拍。经工艺管理部与总装车间反复研讨，决定利用油压机结构制作一套共用压紧工装，包含液压站、油缸、支撑架等部件，通过液压站为油缸提供压力来克服弹簧弹力，使螺栓紧固安装不受弹力影响。该工装投入使用后，作业员只需将产品放置在支撑架上，由油缸压紧座盖，即可轻松完成螺栓紧固与力矩施加，单台产品螺栓安装时间由原来的30分钟缩短至5分钟，同时抬高了操作高度，彻底消除了作业员弯腰下蹲的体力负担。该工装已稳定运行半年有余，为多批次紧急订单的按时交付提供了有力保障。

两款产品内部结构均由两个液压腔和一个冷却腔组成，摩擦组件安装于制动器内部，与以往产品结构差异显著，装配经验几乎无从借鉴。总装车间液压班组面对全新挑战，从零开始摸索共用装配工艺流程，逐步确立了“装活塞—保油压—装摩擦片—装螺栓—装格茨密封件—密封性测试”的标准化作业顺序，并同步确认了多套专用工装的设计要求。其中，新型密封件“格茨密封”的安装技术难度较高，班组成员在厂家培训后迅速掌握关键技术要点，经反复实践验证，密封装配质量稳步提升，后续批量产品泄漏问题得到有效控制，该项成果主要体现在HSPA65产品的批量生产中。在HSPA150250新产品样机装配过程中，班组成员发现原有工装无法同时满足活塞定位与壳体对位的要求，且配合面存在压伤壳体表面的风险，主动提出在工装上增加定位销、定位孔及配合面避开槽的优化方案，经车间与工艺部门确认实施后，既节省了装配时间，又避免了返工返修损失。该优化方案随后推广应用于批量生产，支撑了稳定高效的产品下线节奏。 从工装设计优化到装配流程再造，从技术难点攻克到标准作业固化，工艺管理部与总装车间以协同创新打通了湿式制动器装配瓶颈。通过持续改进，该类产品已逐步实现稳定批量化生产，充分展现了团队在复杂产品工艺攻关中的技术实力与责任担当。

5月7日，国家标准化管理委员会正式批准发布6项风力发电领域国家标准，其中由江西华伍制动器股份有限公司牵头制定的GB/T 47557-2026《风能发电系统 风力发电机组制动系统技术规范》成功落地，标志着我国风力发电机组制动系统领域迎来首个全链条统一技术准则，覆盖并网型风力发电机组制动系统的工作条件、技术要求、试验方法、检验规则以及包装、运输和贮存全流程，明确制动系统的功能性能、结构强度、环境耐受、可靠性及使用寿命等关键指标，充实了风能发电系统国家标准体系。

制动系统是直接关系风电机组运行安全“关键防线”。该标准的实施，将有效筑牢机组超速、失控等重大安全风险防线，从源头提升风电装备安全性和可靠性。同时，引导企业规范研发生产，进一步提升制动装置国产化配套水平与整机运行安全稳定性，为风电场安全运营、行业规范化管理及风电装备产业健康可持续发展提供坚实标准保障。

华伍股份深耕工业制动领域34年，作为行业龙头，市场占有率常年位居首位，已成为金风、远景、明阳、运达、三一、东汽、GE、SIEMENS等国内外主流风电整机企业的核心供应商，产品覆盖20kW至26MW各类风电机型。此次牵头制定国家标准，彰显了公司在风电制动领域的技术权威与行业影响力，也体现了推动行业高质量发展的责任担当。

当前，我国风电产业正迈向高质量发展新阶段，深远海风电开发加速推进，对风电装备安全性、可靠性、标准化水平提出更高要求。公司将以此次标准发布为契机，持续加大研发投入，强化技术创新，不断提升风电制动产品性能与质量，全力推动风电制动技术国产化、标准化、智能化发展，为我国风电产业标准化、绿色化、规范化发展，助力“双碳”战略实施贡献更大华伍力量。

皮带运输机长时间连续运行的设备上，大量使用了电力液压鼓式和盘式制动器。这类设备通常连续工作数周甚至数月，制动器长时间通电保持释放状态，不仅能耗较高，也对配套推动器的使用寿命产生了较大影响。

为适应皮带输送机连续作业的工况要求，公司开发了带电磁铁维持功能的EDM推动器，并配套电控箱。其工作原理为：主控发出制动器释放信号后，电控箱控制推动器电机通电，推杆推出克服弹簧力使制动器释放，开闸限位动作后，系统切换至低能耗的电磁铁维持制动器松闸状态，并延时切断电机电源。由于电磁铁在达到热饱和后进入热稳定状态，功率较低，既实现了节能，又降低了推动器的温升，从而延长了其使用寿命。

随着电子技术的发展，原有电控箱体积较大，现场使用时需布线放线，工作量大。为此，技术中心电气团队开发了一种集成控制单元EDMC。该单元外形紧凑，可与推动器一体安装，能够自动控制制动器从上电开闸到断电抱闸的整个过程。

EDMC的硬件方案设计如下：采用三相交流380V供电，搭载工业级32位MCU；具备干接点信号输入（启动信号、异常强制信号、松闸限位信号等）；提供干接点信号输出（故障信号、松闸反馈信号），以及电磁铁控制信号（DC24V～DC340V/3A可调）；并具备各类故障信号指示功能，同时提供带有故障记录信息查询的TYPE-C接口。

EDMC的主要工作流程为：系统上电后，检测是否存在启动信号，若启动信号有效，则输出三相380V电压，驱动推动器推出，释放制动器，同时通过限位信号判断制动器是否已打开到位。到位后，系统输出电磁铁控制信号，电机延时断电。电磁铁控制信号持续输出，直至外部电源断电或启动信号消失。

相较于传统电控箱，EDMC在以下几个方面具有明显优势：其一，采用一拖一的控制方式，只需接入三相AC380V电源或干接点启动信号即可与甲方控制系统对接，项目实施更加便捷；其二，控制单元体积小巧，通过简易支架即可安装在推动器上，实现制动器一体式安装，便于项目实施与后期维护检修；其三，EDMC为自主设计开发，元器件选型多样化，有效规避了敏感时期可能出现的货源紧张问题；其四，EDMC的设计方向是适配各类类似带电磁铁维持功能的推动器控制，可兼容多种型号电磁铁，无需改变外部供电方式。原有电控方式需单独配备AC220V电源或通过变压器转换获得，现场实施多有不便，EDMC则有效解决了这一痛点。

为积极应对国际管理体系标准的最新变革，全面提升企业合规经营与可持续发展能力，8月20~22日，公司组织开展了ISO 9001:2026质量管理体系与ISO 14001:2026环境管理体系新版标准更新专项培训。

本次培训紧扣时代脉搏与企业实际，特邀华夏健峰咨询公司认证专家授课。专家围绕两大新版标准的修订背景、核心变化及未来发展趋势进行了系统深入的解读。在质量管理体系方面，重点剖析了新版标准在强化风险思维、融入数字化整合以及提升组织韧性等方面的新要求；在环境管理体系方面，深入阐释了从“被动合规”向“主动可持续发展”的战略跃迁，详细讲解了气候变化应对、生物多样性保护及全生命周期供应链管控等新增核心条款。 8月20日，公司各级管理人员及内审员齐聚一堂，共同学习新标准核心要求。为确保体系领导作用原则的有效落地，培训特别安排对管理层涉及的条款进行了逐条剖析。

培训现场学习氛围浓厚。专家不仅对新旧标准差异进行了逐条对比，还结合其他企业的实战案例，生动演示了过程管控与风险思维在日常运营中的落地方法。针对公司高度关注的转版全流程、差距诊断分析、体系文件重构及现场审核重点等实操内容，专家进行了细致指导，并对参训人员在体系运行和换版筹备中遇到的痛点难点进行现场答疑，有效破除认知盲区与实操困惑。

此次培训不仅是一次知识更新，更是一场管理理念的升华。通过系统化学习，参训人员精准掌握了新版标准的核心变动与实施要点，进一步理清了体系升级的工作思路。大家纷纷表示，培训内容干货满满、务实高效，为后续开展差距分析、完善管理制度、优化作业流程奠定了坚实的理论基础。

管理体系的迭代升级是企业迈向高质量发展的必经之路。下一步，公司将以此次培训为契机，全面启动新版标准的转版筹备工作，对照新标准开展差距诊断与文件修订，坚持一体化整合思路，杜绝“两张皮”现象。同时，将新标准要求深度融入日常运营与战略决策，以标准化建设赋能数字化转型与规范化发展，不断完善公司管理体系，为公司长远稳健发展保驾护航。

七月盛夏，骄阳似火，华伍厂区内却涌动着一股沁人心脾的清凉。7月17日，一箱箱脆甜多汁的梨子与一袋袋沉甸甸的大米被有序发放到每位员工手中；时隔不到一周，又一批新鲜翠绿的西瓜如期而至。这份接连不断的夏日关怀，正是华伍“家园文化”在平凡日常中最朴素、也最真实的注脚。

在华伍三十余年的发展历程中，“家”的理念始终是凝聚人心、推动企业行稳致远的精神内核。从创业初期的同甘共苦，到上市后的现代化治理转型，这份“家园文化”在传承中不断发展，成为企业应对挑战、再创辉煌的隐形引擎。企业与员工休戚与共、共同奋斗，这便是“家园文化”最质朴的初心。

“家园文化”从来不只是挂在嘴边的口号，而是落实到每一个具体行动中的温度。从2017年占地3300平方米的“职工之家”综合文体场馆落成，到三栋员工宿舍楼的全面翻新；从上下班通勤厂车的暖心接送，到厂区内50辆便民自行车的投放；从坚持了十多年的“金秋奖学”活动，到传统佳节里从不缺席的节日礼品……点点滴滴汇聚成华伍人对“家”的归属感。更值得一提的是，公司每月都会为过生日的员工送上一张购物卡，虽是一份小小的礼物，却让每一位华伍人在属于自己的特别日子里，感受到来自“家”的惦记与祝福。这些看似琐碎的细节，恰恰构成了“家”最动人的底色。

真正的“家园文化”，不仅要让员工感受到温暖，更要让员工分享到企业发展的红利。公司先后实施两期员工持股计划，覆盖母公司及子公司员工数百人，通过非公开发行股票、回购股份等方式，让一线员工真正成为企业的主人。2026年7月，董事长再次提议回购公司股份用于员工持股或股权激励，持续践行“企业增效、员工增收”的利益共享理念。这种“家”的认同感，最终将转化为强大的组织凝聚力。

从盛夏的一口西瓜、一箱梨子，到员工宿舍里的一台空调、一辆便民自行车；从职级晋升的成长通道，到员工持股的利益共享——华伍的“家园文化”既有柴米油盐的烟火气，也有共同奋斗的使命感。三十余年风雨同行，华伍用温暖凝聚人心，用事业激励前行，在奔向百年品牌的征程中，这份“家”的力量，正成为企业最坚固的精神根基，也是未来道路上最温暖、最持久的力量。

6月25日至26日，江西华伍制动器股份有限公司车工职业技能等级自主认定考试在公司内部顺利举行。来自车间的一线车工齐聚考场，按照各自申报等级分别完成了五级和四级的考核。参考队伍中新老搭配，既有深耕岗位十余年的技术能手，也有崭露头角的青年骨干。本次考试严格对标国家职业技能标准组织实施，丰城就业中心外部质量督导团队亲临现场全程监督，保障了考核流程的规范性与等级证书的权威有效性。

职业技能等级企业自主认定，是国家技能人才评价“放管服”改革的重要落地举措。该政策面向一线技能员工，由企业结合生产实际自主组织考核，考核通过后核发的技能等级证书国家认可、全国通用，是个人专业技能的权威证明。依托这一政策支持，公司将技能等级认定与员工岗位能力提升、职业发展成长深度结合，构建起“技能培养—等级认证—能力进阶”的完整发展体系。考核标准紧密贴合车间生产实际，等级认定精准匹配岗位成长需求，真正为一线员工打通了凭手艺进阶、靠技能成才的职业发展通道。

本次认定分为理论知识考试与实操技能考核两大环节，全面检验参考员工的专业功底与实操水平。理论考场纪律严明，员工沉着应答，扎实检验了自身的专业知识储备。实操考核现场，车床平稳运转，参考员工屏气凝神，从图纸核对、量具校准，到工件装夹、切削加工、精度检测，每一步都严格遵照工艺规范执行。考评组对照国家职业技能标准，对操作流程、工件精度、作业规范逐项打分，确保考核结果客观公正。

为保障考试顺利实施，公司提前统筹各项考务工作，组建了专业考评队伍，全流程把控考核质量。考试期间，丰城就业中心督导人员对考务筹备、考场管理、考评执行、质量管控等环节进行了全流程监督检查，对公司规范严谨的组织工作给予了充分肯定，同时也对后续认定工作的标准化优化提出了专业指导。

开展职业技能等级自主认定，是公司支持一线员工成长、夯实技能人才队伍的重要举措。既为一线员工提供了官方认可的能力认证平台，也为公司持续发展积蓄了坚实的技能力量。下一步，公司将持续用好政策支持，逐步拓宽技能认定的工种覆盖范围，完善配套培养机制，落实技能等级与薪酬待遇挂钩的激励制度，充分调动一线员工钻研技术、提升技能的积极性，让更多岗位的员工成长有通道、付出有回报，持续壮大公司高素质技能人才队伍，支撑企业实现持续稳健发展。

4月25日，丰城市首届“华伍杯”羽毛球混合团体赛在畅翔羽毛球馆火热开赛并圆满收官。本次赛事由华伍股份主办、丰城市羽毛球协会承办，共集结6支队伍同台竞技，参赛选手既有华伍股份各部门员工，也有丰城市羽毛球协会的专业爱好者，以羽球为纽带搭建起政企文体交流的平台。

6支队伍的队名均源自华伍三十余年的发展历程与核心主业——从工业制动主业到风电战略业务，从工匠精神到安全使命，每一个队名都镌刻着华伍人的精神印记。赛事设置五个竞赛项目，采用上下半区分组循环赛制，上午进行小组循环赛，下午展开半决赛与冠军争夺战。赛事秉持“人人皆有登场之机”的原则，采用31分制直落决胜。

赛场上，男双对抗激烈，大力扣杀与快速攻防频频上演；混双搭档配合默契，攻防轮转行云流水；女双选手稳扎稳打，凭借精准落点控制打出多场精彩对决。选手们全情投入，场边助威声此起彼伏，现场氛围热烈融洽。小组赛阶段，各队打法特色鲜明：华风队快攻凌厉，华匠队细腻沉稳，华领队排兵布阵从容有度，华制队攻防兼备，均给观众留下深刻印象。

经过激烈角逐，华安队、华锐队、华匠队、华风队凭借总积分优势晋级四强。半决赛中，华安队凭借稳健发挥与默契配合顺利拿下决赛席位；华锐队则火力全开，以凌厉攻势锁定另一张决赛入场券。最终，华安队勇夺冠军，华锐队斩获亚军，华匠队获得季军，华风队获得殿军。

本次赛事秉持“独乐乐不如众乐乐”的初心，胜负之外更重同乐，让大家在赛场上“赢则同狂，输亦共扛”，尽情展现团队风采。全体裁判员公正执裁，运动员赛出水平、赛出风范，不仅搭建了切磋交流的平台，也让大家在紧张工作之余放松身心，在团队协作中增进凝聚力。后续公司将持续开展丰富多样的文体活动，引导大家以更饱满的状态投入工作与生活，为企业发展和家乡建设注入更多活力。

李智，男，汉族，中共党员，江西永新人，1987年9月出生，2017年10月加入中国共产党，大学本科学历，江西华伍制动器股份有限公司铸造车间主任，技师（铸造熔炼浇注工）。工作十余年来，他扎根热加工领域，潜心钻研，勇于创新，先后获评“宜春工匠”“中国机械工业百名工匠”“江西省新时代赣鄱先锋—群众身边好党员”“江西铸造技术能手”等荣誉，在全国铸造行业技能竞赛中屡创佳绩，并当选江西省机械工程学会铸造分会常务理事。

面对风电关键部件长期受制于人的困境，李智同志牢记“国之大者”，主动扛起自主创新重任。2011年，公司启动风电制动器低温球墨铸铁件国产化项目，作为铸造车间首位员工，他带领团队从零起步，自主构建工艺体系、编制全套技术标准。历经数百次试验，成功突破材料成分设计、组织凝固控制等核心技术壁垒，实现该“卡脖子”部件从依赖进口到完全自主的跨越，助力公司成为国内主流风电主机厂核心供应商。针对行业公认的“高抗拉强度+高延伸率+优异低温冲击韧性”技术难题，他跨界钻研冶金与材料科学，成功开发两个具有自主知识产权的新型铸铁牌号，为装备轻量化开辟新路径。他坚持将个人成果转化为集体财富，围绕“派普树脂砂皮下气孔”等行业罕见缺陷撰写并公开发表技术论文，无私分享经验。通过持续优化工艺，他将铸件出品率由69.8%提升至87.6%，年节约成本超200万元；改进下芯方式与过滤系统，年降本十余万元。2021年底，他主导完成通用电气（GE）全球供应商严苛审核，推动企业加速打入国际市场，以硬核技术诠释了共产党员的责任担当。

李智同志始终坚信：“一个人走得快，一群人才能走得远。”作为党员技术骨干，他把培养青年人才视为政治责任。坚持每日深入一线，“手把手”传授模具开发、工艺调试等核心技艺；利用工余时间自编培训教材，将复杂原理转化为生动案例，累计培养技术骨干十余名，多人已成长为岗位能手。他创新推行车间独立核算与绩效联动机制，组织团队签订责任状，通过流程再造与技术创新，在产量屡创历史新高的同时，实现年度盈利超千万元，真正实现企业增效、员工增收的双赢局面。同事们评价他“随叫随到、毫无保留”，在他的带动下，一支政治过硬、技术精湛、作风扎实的高技能团队迅速成长，为企业高质量发展注入源源不断的红色动能。

“党员的身份不是光环，而是责任。”这是李智常挂在嘴边的话。在疫情防控最严峻时期，公司实行封闭管理，他第一时间驻厂值守，主动协调解决同事食宿困难，腾出个人物资支援一线，搭建临时休息区，并组织文体活动稳定队伍情绪，确保车间“零感染、生产不断链”。十余年来，他始终扎根生产一线，从普通技术员成长为行业专家，身份在变，但“干在实处、走在前列”的初心从未改变。他没有惊天动地的壮举，却用日复一日的专注、创新、求精与奉献，在平凡岗位上默默践行着入党誓词。他以实际行动诠释了新时代共产党员“平常时候看得出来、关键时刻站得出来、危难关头豁得出来”的先锋形象，赢得了干部职工的广泛赞誉。

李智的奋斗之路，是匠心与初心的辉映。他以风电部件为画卷，用精确的参数和创新的思维描绘着现代工业之美；更以共产党员的忠诚与担当为底色，在熔炉的炽热与数据的冷静间，淬炼出新时代产业先锋的纯粹本色。他的足迹，深深印刻在铸造技术高质量发展的征途上，激励着更多奋斗者勇毅前行，共同谱写中国制造的时代华章。

Partnership brings Bosch’s technology leadership to the Summit’s dedicated Global Mobility Insights Session, as senior mobility leaders gather in Korea to explore the complexities of mobility

LONDON, UK / SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA, FISITA, the global alliance advancing the technology of mobility, today announced that Bosch Korea has signed on as the exclusive Global Mobility Insights Partner for the FISITA World Mobility Summit 2026. The Summit takes place 4–5 November 2026 at the Rolling Hills Hotel in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi, Republic of Korea, hosted by FISITA in partnership with the Korean Society of Automotive Engineers (KSAE).

As Global Mobility Insights Partner, Bosch Korea will sponsor the Summit’s dedicated Global Mobility Insights Session, contributing to one of the event’s most important dialogues on the future direction of mobility technology and engineering. The partnership reflects Bosch’s long-standing commitment to innovation, collaboration and thought leadership across the global mobility ecosystem.

Hosted by FISITA President ChangHwan Kim, Executive Vice President of Hyundai Motor Company and held under the theme “Embracing the Complexities of Mobility,” the 2026 Summit is FISITA’s annual leadership forum, bringing together senior executives, CTOs and R&D leaders from the world’s most significant automotive and mobility organisations, including Hyundai Motor Group, Toyota, Xiaomi Auto and Bosch, alongside the presidents of FISITA’s member engineering societies.

Over two days of strategic discussion, thought leadership and high-level networking, delegates will examine the strategic forces shaping mobility’s future, including software-defined vehicles and AI, battery technology and electrification, energy infrastructure, autonomous driving and regulation and regional perspectives from Asia, Europe and North America.

Recognised as one of the most exclusive gatherings in the international mobility leadership calendar, the FISITA World Mobility Summit provides a unique environment for senior executives, engineers, researchers and industry decision-makers to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions and explore practical pathways towards a safe, sustainable and affordable mobility future.

“We are delighted to welcome Bosch Korea as our Global Mobility Insights Partner for the FISITA World Mobility Summit 2026. Bosch is recognised worldwide for its engineering excellence, technology leadership and commitment to advancing mobility innovation and having them join us is a real vote of confidence in what this Summit is built to do, bring the industry’s most significant decision-makers into one room, in Korea, to work through the questions that matter most”

– Chris Mason, Chief Executive Officer, FISITA.

“The Summit is intentionally designed to bring together the people responsible for making some of the most important decisions in global mobility and partnerships like this are exactly what allow us to keep raising the bar for what it delivers, for our members and for the wider industry.”

“The future of mobility will not be defined by a single technology, a single company or a single market, success will depend on our ability to embrace complexity and bring together expertise from across the entire mobility ecosystem. That belief sits at the heart of the FISITA World Mobility Summit 2026 and it is exactly why I am so pleased to welcome Bosch Korea as our Global Mobility Insights Partner”

– ChangHwan Kim, President, FISITA and Executive Vice President, Hyundai Motor Company

“Bosch’s presence in this session reflects the kind of cross-industry collaboration our sector needs. As we explore topics ranging from software-defined vehicles and AI to battery technologies, automated driving and energy infrastructure, the complexity we face is not a problem to be eliminated, it is a reality to be embraced together and that is what we will do in Korea this November.”

“Bosch is proud to support the FISITA World Mobility Summit 2026 as Global Mobility Insights Partner. The Summit has established itself as one of the most respected forums for senior technology leaders across the global mobility community, exactly the audience we want to be in dialogue with as the industry sets the direction for the next generation of mobility,”

“The theme ‘Embracing the Complexities of Mobility’ strongly reflects the realities facing our industry today. Delivering sustainable, safe and intelligent mobility requires collaboration across technologies, industries and regions and we look forward to contributing our insights and engaging with industry peers in Korea this November.”

– Marcello Lusuardi, President of Robert Bosch Korea.

Other organisations attending the FISITA World Mobility Summit include: BYD, Changan, Denso, JATCO, Maersk, Mann+Hummel, NIO, Toyota Motor Corporation, Xiaomi and Geely.

Further details on the FISITA World Mobility Summit 2026, including registration and the full programme, are available at www.fisita.com/summit

A reflection on leadership, collaboration and the relentless pursuit of progress, for industry, people, and planet, by Chris Mason, CEO, FISITA

When Alan Mulally took the helm at Ford in 2006, the company was haemorrhaging billions. What he brought with him wasn’t a rescue plan in the conventional sense. It was a philosophy: ‘Working Together’ – one team, one plan with total transparency, and the radical idea that transformation happens not through individual brilliance but through people choosing to work genuinely and consistently with each other.

I’ve been thinking about that a lot lately, because 12 years at FISITA will do that to you.

Twelve years of watching the mobility landscape shift beneath our feet, 12 years of convening engineers, executives and researchers from across the globe, and 12 years of becoming increasingly convinced that the lesson Mulally taught Ford is the same lesson the entire mobility ecosystem needs to internalise right now.

The world has changed, but the need for alliance has not

When I joined FISITA, electrification was a conviction held by relatively few, automated driving was a research topic, and the software-defined vehicle was a concept paper. Today, each of these is a contested, complex, racing reality and none of them respects national borders or organisational silos.

Transformation happens not through individual brilliance, but through people choosing to genuinely work with each other

The challenges of the mobility transition are genuinely global; a regulation shaped in Brussels affects a supplier in Seoul, a battery chemistry breakthrough in Shanghai reshapes a manufacturing strategy in Sunderland, an AI capability developed in Silicon Valley raises safety questions that engineers in Tokyo need to answer.

This is precisely why FISITA exists – not to advocate for any one technology, company or geography but to actively promote co-operation between the brilliant minds working across all of them. In a world that sometimes pulls towards insularity, we remain resolutely, unashamedly global.

The pre-competitive space is where the real work happens

One of the most valuable and least celebrated spaces in any industry is the pre-competitive space. The place where competitors sit in the same room, set aside market dynamics and ask: ‘What do we need to figure out together, for the good of all of us and the people we ultimately serve?’

Mulally called it ‘having a compelling vision that everyone understands and is aligned to.’ FISITA calls it our international technology of mobility alliance. I have seen, across 12 years of convening these conversations, what happens when the right people are in the same room without a competitive agenda; standards get shaped and safety frameworks get built, young engineers get connected to mentors who change their careers, and the future of mobility – which belongs to all of us – gets a little clearer.

The pre-competitive space is where the future gets built. It’s where we choose progress over positioning

That is what FISITA’s collaborative model makes possible, and it is something I have never taken for granted.

Leadership in a transition era means enabling others

The mobility transition is the largest industrial transformation of our generation. It is also one of the most contested, technically, commercially and politically. In this environment, I think leadership means something different to what it once did.

It doesn’t mean having all the answers, it means creating the conditions for the right questions to be asked, by the right people, with the rigour and openness they deserve.

FISITA’s ‘Enabling’ value is the one I return to most in this context. Our role is to make the right conversations happen at the right time and to ensure that thought leadership in this space is both expert and genuinely forward-looking, and not just a platform for whoever shouts loudest.

Mulally understood that a leader’s job is to serve the team, to give people clarity, confidence and connection, and to hold to the plan when the pressure to abandon it is immense. Twelve years at FISITA have taught me that the same is true of an organisation like ours; we are not here to lead mobility’s future, we are here to enable the people who will.

The next decade of mobility will be defined by decisions made in the next three to five years, on software architecture, on safety standards for automated systems, on battery technology pathways and on how we regulate AI when it’s making decisions at 70mph.

These decisions require the full diversity of the global mobility ecosystem, engineers and ethicists, policymakers and practitioners, established manufacturers and ambitious new entrants. They require exactly the kind of inclusive, expert, purposeful dialogue that FISITA has been facilitating for over 70 years.

The next chapter is already taking shape. In November, we gather in Seoul for the FISITA World Mobility Summit , hosted by FISITA President ChangHwan Kim and the team at Hyundai, to do exactly this work: connecting the voices shaping intelligent safety, automated driving and carbon neutral mobility. Then, in June 2027, we will bring the global community to Barcelona for the FISITA World Mobility Conference 2027 .

Twelve years in, I am more convinced than ever that our model – global, collaborative, enabling – is not just relevant, it is essential.

Working together isn’t a nice-to-have for the mobility transition; it’s the only way through it.

For too long, industry conversations have been framed as either/or debates. Is it battery electric or hydrogen? Software or hardware solutions? Autonomous or human-led? Global platforms or regional solutions? But the reality facing mobility leaders today is far more nuanced.

As FISITA President I believe that the challenges confronting our industry are too significant to be solved in isolation. They require collaboration across disciplines, geographies and technologies, bringing together different perspectives to create meaningful progress.

The future of mobility is not a binary choice; it is an integrated portfolio of solutions, evolving at different speeds, across different markets, to meet different societal, environmental and commercial needs. Those needs range from providing safe, accessible and affordable mobility for growing and ageing populations, to reducing emissions and resource consumption, while ensuring businesses can remain competitive, resilient and profitable in a rapidly changing global market. The decisions we make today will shape not only how people and goods move, but also the environmental legacy, economic opportunities and quality of life inherited by future generations. Progress is therefore not simply an industry ambition, it is our responsibility.

The decisions we make today will shape not only how people and goods move, but also the environmental legacy, economic opportunities and quality of life inherited by future generations.

Battery technologies will continue to advance; hydrogen will play an important role; software-defined vehicles and AI are reshaping development cycles; automated driving will arrive through varying levels of deployment and regulation; energy infrastructure will develop unevenly across regions. None of these exist in isolation and they are interconnected parts of a much larger system.

This complexity is not a problem to be eliminated; it is a reality to be embraced.

That is why the theme of the FISITA World Mobility Summit 2026 is “Embracing the Complexities of Mobility.” The Summit will bring together senior technology and engineering leaders from the world’s most influential mobility organisations.

FISITA’s unique community brings together global industry leaders and representatives of engineering societies that collectively connect engineers, researchers and mobility professionals across every major region of the world. It creates a rare environment where leaders can move beyond headlines, challenge assumptions, and explore practical pathways forward.

For organisations looking to shape the conversation, now is the time to engage. Whether through attendance, exhibition participation or partnership, there are only a limited number of opportunities to be part of this highly curated gathering of decision-makers and influencers from across the global mobility ecosystem.

The industry’s biggest challenges will not be solved by choosing one path over another. They will be solved by bringing the right people together to understand how multiple pathways can work together. That’s the conversation we need to have.

ChangHwan Kim, President, FISITA Executive Vice President, Hyundai Motor Company

For more information about the 2026 FISITA World Mobility Summit visit www.fisita.com/summit

Circular economy solutions are no longer optional – they are essential in a world of finite resources, writes Sophie Schmidtlin.

The circular economy is rapidly becoming a central strategic pillar of transformation for the automotive sector. This shift is driven by tighter regulatory requirements, increasing pressure on raw material supply, the transition to electromobility, and the industrialization of reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling value chains.

As Chair of the FISITA Circular Economy Expert Group and CTO of The Future is NEUTRAL , I see first-hand the depth and momentum of this transformation across the industry.

A closer look at the world of automotive circularity

Europe is currently the most advanced continent in automotive circular economy. Its leadership is rooted in a binding and systemic regulatory framework that now fully embraces a “circular by design” approach. This ambition is reinforced by a relatively mature industrial ecosystem, with several actors already operating at scale across reuse, remanufacturing, and closed-loop material recycling.

Asia-Pacific is following Europe’s lead through a different route: industrial power and speed of execution rather than regulation. China, Japan, India, and South Korea are accelerating circular initiatives at scale, driven by resource security, electrification, and strong capabilities in manufacturing, dismantling, and battery recovery.

Europe is currently the most advanced continent in automotive circular economy. Its leadership fully embraces a “circular by design” approach

By contrast, North America remains more limited from a regulatory perspective, although remanufacturing has long been deeply embedded in its automotive ecosystem. Circularity there progresses mainly through market forces, such as cost optimisation, supply chain resilience, and ESG commitments.

Other regions, including Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East, still play a marginal role in global automotive circularity. They are often positioned as second-life vehicle markets, informal dismantling territories, or low-value secondary material pools, rather than as fully integrated circular ecosystems.

From end-of-life vehicle handling to circular design

End-of-life vehicle (ELV) management represents the historical backbone of automotive circular economy. In France, approximately 1.2 million ELVs are processed every year by nearly 1,700 accredited treatment centres. Across Europe, around 11 million ELVs are generated annually, forming the primary resource base of automotive circularity.

Since 2015, European regulation has required that at least 85 percent of an ELV be reused or recycled, and 95 percent be reused, recycled, or recovered (including energy recovery). These targets measure the performance of the ELV treatment chain after dismantling, shredding, sorting, and material processing.

Circularity cannot succeed in isolation; cross-industry and cross-border collaboration is essential, and leadership increasingly means the ability to orchestrate ecosystems

Yet a structural paradox remains: despite high theoretical recyclability, new vehicles today still contain less than 30% recycled materials. Most of this comes from post-industrial metal scrap; only marginal shares come from post-consumer plastics, and very little from ELVs themselves. In short, cars are designed to be recyclable but are still largely produced from virgin materials.

France was a regulatory pioneer with the AGEC law (Anti-Waste Law for a Circular Economy) in 2020. It created an automotive Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme, effective since 2024, introducing free ELV take-back, stronger traceability, and reinforced action against so-called “missing vehicles.”

This approach is now scaling up through the forthcoming EU ELV Regulation, which is expected to enter into force by mid-2026. Directly applicable across all EU Member States, it will strengthen dismantlability and recyclability requirements, improve vehicle and parts traceability, and consolidate the economic role of reuse and remanufacturing. Its scope will also extend to new categories, including heavy-duty vehicles and two-wheelers.

End-of-life is thus becoming an upstream strategic lever, directly influencing vehicle design and engineering choices.

The Future is NEUTRAL: An operational circular model

The Future is NEUTRAL is a reference player in automotive circular economy and the only actor offering competitive solutions across the entire automotive ecosystem: manufacturers, suppliers, insurers, repairers, and private customers.

Its ambition is to act as a growth engine for the sector by delivering true “Car-to-Car” solutions. Its integrated circular value chain starts with ELV collection, depollution, and dismantling, followed by direct reuse or remanufacturing of high-value components. Non-reusable materials, such as metals, plastics, and batteries are recycled through dedicated industrial processes. Reconditioned parts and recycled materials are reinjected directly into vehicle production and aftersales, reducing costs, emissions, and dependency on virgin resources.

A structural paradox remains: despite high theoretical recyclability, new vehicles today still contain less than 30% recycled materials

This model demonstrates that circular economy can simultaneously enhance environmental performance, resource security, and economic resilience.

One of the strongest messages emerging from this transition is the evolving role of automotive engineers. Performance and cost remain essential, but as standalone metrics they are no longer sufficient. Engineers are becoming architects of circular systems, integrating eco-design, modularity, repairability, and recyclability from the earliest stages.

The agenda for EuroBrake 2025 was designed to explore the full spectrum of braking technologies, from braking materials and NVH to brake-by-wire, thermal management, validation, and automated braking systems. The programme included 21 technical sessions, with high level presentations from leading experts, inspiring keynote speeches, a vibrant OEM panel and a dedicated strategy panel focusing on global innovations and challenges in vehicle braking systems.

Through the 2025 EuroBrake Student Opportunity Programme we once again welcomed 15 talented international students to our community. And for the first time we proudly awarded the Harald Abendroth Prize to recognise the work of the next generation of engineers.

Foreword: Jan Münchhoff, Chair, EuroBrake 2025

We hope you enjoy this review of EuroBrake 2025. To learn more about EuroBrake, please contact FISITA —the EuroBrake community would welcome your contribution.

contents.https://www.bosch-presse.de/pressportal/: Stuttgart, Germany – The Bosch Group posted solid results in the first half of 2026 amid a business environment that remains challenging. The supplier of technology and services increased its sales revenue by 3.6 percent to 46.4 billion euros (H1 2025: 44.8 billion euros). The HVAC business recently acquired from Johnson Controls and Hitachi contributed some 2 billion euros in sales growth. EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) from operations stood at 2.2 billion euros (H1 2025: 2.3 billion euros). The EBIT margin from operations was 4.6 percent of sales revenue, compared with 5.1 percent in the previous year. Result was primarily impacted by special effects in the Mobility business. Despite numerous economic and geopolitical uncertainties, Bosch is reaffirming its forecast of sales and result for the full year. “With solid sales growth in the first half of the year, we see ourselves on the home stretch for 2026, but we still need a strong finish,” said Markus Forschner , the chief financial officer and deputy chairman of the board of management of Robert Bosch GmbH, while presenting half-year figures for the first time. “That is why we are steadfastly pursuing the structural adjustments and cost-cutting measures we have initiated, so that we can continue to make major upfront investments in emerging technologies and capitalize on growth opportunities.”

Stuttgart, Germany and Madrid, Spain – In Europe, pressure on urban public transit is mounting: in light of mandatory EU requirements to reduce carbon emissions from city buses by 90 percent by 2030, public transit operators are seeking reliable, emissions-free solutions. To this end, an initial test operation is now launching in Madrid: Equipped with a fuel-cell power module (FCPM) from Bosch, an Irizar bus has been transporting passengers through the Spanish capital for several weeks now. Vehicle operation will focus on routes where the fuel cell’s long range allows it to fully demonstrate its advantages. The operator is the Spanish bus company Alsa.

Stuttgart – Prof. Christof Ehrhart (60) is leaving Bosch on December 31, 2026, at his own request to pursue commitments and projects outside the company. In his capacity as the company’s head of communications, he has been responsible worldwide for internal and external communications, governmental affairs, relations with industry associations and stakeholder groups, and strategic brand management since 2019. Ehrhart can look back on three decades of leadership roles in international communications. In 2024, he received the prestigious German Image Award for the second time for his communications work at Bosch.

Stuttgart – Bosch, in collaboration with Toyota Motor Europe, BMW Group and Repsol, today announces the launch of a pioneering six-month pilot project in Spain. The pilot, which started in early July, will demonstrate the real-world potential of Vehicles running Exclusively on Eligible Fuels (VEEF)*. The initiative will deploy a fleet of around 20 Toyota and BMW vehicles, powered by Repsol’s 100 % renewable gasoline (Nexa 95), and supported by Bosch’s advanced digital fuel tracking technology. This pilot aims to provide tangible, real-world evidence that vehicles exclusively running on eligible fuels can be effectively deployed at scale, supporting Europe’s transition to decarbonize mobility through a complementary, technology-neutral approach while leaving no one behind.

Stuttgart – The following personnel changes are taking place on the board of management of Robert Bosch GmbH:

Dr. Stefan Hartung is stepping down from his position as chairman of the board of management effective June 30, 2026, at his own request and in close consultation and agreement with the shareholders. He is thus leaving the board of management and that of Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG. His successor as of July 1, 2026 will be Dr. Christian Fischer . Dr. Markus Forschner and Dr. Markus Heyn will be appointed vice chairmen of the board of management.

As CEO of Bosch, Stefan Hartung has strongly driven the company’s development and consistently focused it on growth and innovation. During very challenging times and under difficult conditions, Hartung achieved important milestones for the company’s future viability and competitiveness. In future, he plans to dedicate his time to new social commitments and entrepreneurial tasks outside the Bosch Group. “The shareholders and the supervisory board regret Stefan Hartung’s decision and express their sincere gratitude to him for his outstanding achievements in the diligent management of the company during an exceptionally challenging period,” said Prof. Stefan Asenkerschbaumer , managing partner of Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG and chairman of the supervisory board of Robert Bosch GmbH.

“As chairman of the board of management, he has driven the strong development of Bosch with purpose, in line with the will of our founder. We respect Stefan Hartung’s personal decision and wish him every success in the future.”

Hartung, who holds a PhD in mechanical engineering, has been a member of the Bosch board of management since 2013 and has served as chairman of the board of management since January 1, 2022. He joined Bosch und Siemens Hausgeräte GmbH in Munich in 2004. Prior to that, he had worked at the Fraunhofer Gesellschaft, among other organizations.

Dr. Christian Fischer (58) will succeed Stefan Hartung (60) effective July 1, 2026. As deputy chairman of the board of management and limited partner of Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG, he has already played a key role in shaping the company’s strategic development in recent years. In addition to his responsibility for the Consumer Goods business sector, Fischer has also been in charge of the company’s key growth initiatives, portfolio management, and the development of the company’s senior leadership, among other tasks. Under his leadership, Bosch has expanded and sustainably strengthened its portfolio through the acquisition of the heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) business from Johnson Controls and Hitachi – the largest acquisition in the company’s history. “Christian Fischer has demonstrated in recent years that he thinks strategically, acts with an entrepreneurial mindset, and leads with foresight. Working alongside Stefan Hartung, he has helped shape the company’s fundamental direction and set the course for its transformation. He will consistently drive the implementation of the strategy forward, aiming to future-proof the company amid the multiple challenges in the markets in which it operates,” said Asenkerschbaumer.

Christian Fischer, who holds a PhD in economics, began his professional career in 1996 at Bosch as a trainee. Prior to returning to the company and joining the Bosch board of management in 2018, he held various leadership roles outside the company. Among other achievements, he grew Smartrac – an RFID technology company – from a young start-up into a TecDAX-listed global market leader while serving as its CEO from 2006 to 2012.

To ensure that Bosch’s transformation continues consistently in a forward-looking manner, responsibilities within the board of management will be reorganized as part of the leadership transition. The two members of the board of management Dr. Markus Forschner and Dr. Markus Heyn will be appointed deputy chairmen of the Bosch board of management effective July 1, 2026.

Markus Forschner (59) has served as the company’s chief financial officer (CFO) since 2022 and has been with Bosch since 1996. He studied computer science and business administration and gained a PhD from Stuttgart University’s institute for R&D management. “As an experienced CFO, Markus Forschner stands for financial stability, long-term thinking, and the disciplined execution of the transformation initiatives already adopted. In his new role, he will balance investments in future-oriented fields with financial strength, while maintaining a clear focus on safeguarding the company’s independence,” said Asenkerschbaumer.

Markus Heyn (61) has served as chairman of the Mobility business sector since 2022. He has successfully driven the reorganization of the Mobility sector and is consistently continuing to align the business with future demands. He holds a PhD in mechanical engineering, joined the Bosch Group in 1999, and has been a member of the board of management since 2015. Asenkerschbaumer: “Going forward, Markus Heyn will bring the technology perspective to the group’s senior leadership. As an engineer and head of the company’s largest business sector, Mobility, he represents innovative strength, manufacturing excellence, global market expertise, and has a proven track record in transforming the mobility business.”

The shareholders and the supervisory board wish Christian Fischer, Markus Forschner, and Markus Heyn every success in their new roles.

Continental continued its positive momentum in the second quarter of 2026. Continental sells one of Australia’s largest tyre, automotive service and repair chains to Chinese automotive service platform Tuhu, subject to regulatory approvals

Through its own distribution network Continental has a strong market presence in Australia and will continue to work with mycar Tyre & Auto as a distribution partner

Dalibor Kalina, head of the tyre business in the Asia-Pacific region: “mycar Tyre & Auto has developed very successfully under the Continental umbrella and is now exceptionally well positioned in the Australian market”

Min Chen, founder and CEO of Tuhu: “Australia is a highly attractive and promising market for automotive services, we look forward to building on mycar Tyre & Auto’s strong foundation and bringing Tuhu’s capabilities and experience to the Australian market”

Sydney, September 24, 2026. Continental has announced the sale of its subsidiary mycar Tyre & Auto, one of the largest tyre, automotive service and repair chains in Australia, to Tuhu, a leading Chinese automotive service platform. The transaction is based on an enterprise value of 403 million Australian dollars (approx. 250 million euros). The transaction marks another step in Continental’s strategic focus on its core business to develop and manufacture tyres. Under Tuhu’s ownership, mycar Tyre & Auto will have an owner with a strong focus on automotive services, providing a solid platform for the business to continue its growth and realise its potential. All of the more than 1,600 employees and around 280 stores of mycar Tyre & Auto are part of the transaction, which is subject to regulatory approvals.

“mycar Tyre & Auto has developed very successfully under the Continental umbrella and is now exceptionally well positioned in the Australian market,” said Dalibor Kalina, head of Continental’s tyre business in the Asia-Pacific region. “In Tuhu, mycar Tyre & Auto is gaining an owner with many years of experience who will actively drive the company’s strategic direction and sustainable long-term development. Tuhu and Continental have a long-standing and strong strategic partnership in China. With our own sales organisation in Australia and the continued distribution of our tyres through the mycar Tyre & Auto network, we will ensure seamless continuity for our customers,” Kalina added.

“Australia is a highly attractive and promising market for automotive services, and mycar Tyre & Auto is a distinctive business with a strong position in this market,” said Min Chen, founder and CEO of Tuhu. “We look forward to working closely with the existing management team and employees, while continuing our long-standing partnership with Continental. As a new entrant to the Australian market from China, we are committed to adapting quickly to the local market and building on mycar’s strong foundation established under Continental’s management and its proven track record of responsible and reliable operations. By bringing Tuhu’s capabilities and experience to Australia, we look forward to continuing to deliver value, choice and convenience for Australian vehicle owners,” he added.

Successful expansion of distribution in Australia

Continental acquired mycar Tyre & Auto in 2018 to expand its distribution network in Australia and strengthen its global presence in the tyre market. Since the acquisition, Australia has developed into an established and important market for the company. At the same time, Continental has built its own strong and highly capable sales organisation in Australia over recent years.

Under Continental’s ownership, mycar Tyre & Auto has steadily strengthened its market position in Australia over the past eight years through an expanded store network, a broader product portfolio and an enhanced market presence. The partnership between Continental and Tuhu creates opportunities for closer cooperation in the future. Following the completion of the transaction, mycar Tyre & Auto will remain a distribution partner of Continental in Australia and will continue to sell Continental tires there.

With around 280 stores across Australia, mycar Tyre & Auto offers a comprehensive range of automotive services, including scheduled maintenance, tyres, brakes, suspension, batteries and general mechanical repairs. The company has more than 1,600 employees in Australia, making mycar one of the largest employers in the automotive service and repair industry.

Tuhu is a leading automotive service platform in China and operates the world's largest automotive service network by the store number under management, while serving the largest user base among automotive service platforms in China. As of June 30, 2026, Tuhu's service network comprised 8,825 Tuhu Workshops, and it had approximately 31 million transacting users during the twelve months ending June 30, 2026. Through its integrated online and offline model, Tuhu addresses a broad range of automotive service needs, including tyre and chassis-component replacement, vehicle maintenance and repair, detailing and other related services.

New Conti Eco HT 5 completes Continental's Conti Eco Generation 5 portfolio for steer, drive and trailer axles

Trailer tire designed to support fuel efficiency through lower rolling resistance

High mileage, even wear and reliable performance across varying operating conditions

Coordinated tire solution helps fleets reduce operating costs across the truck and trailer combination

Hanover, Germany, September 22, 2026. Continental is introducing the new Conti Eco HT 5 trailer tire, completing its fifth-generation Conti Eco portfolio for freight transport. Together with the Conti Eco HS 5 steer tire and Conti Eco HD 5 drive tire, it provides fleets with a coordinated solution that combines lower operating costs, high mileage and reduced rolling resistance that can help improve fuel efficiency. Developed for regional and long-distance transport operations, the Conti Eco HT 5 extends the benefits of the Conti Eco Generation 5 family to the trailer axle. While trailer tires are not driven, they account for a significant share of the rolling resistance of a truck and trailer combination. Lower rolling resistance at the trailer axle can help reduce fuel consumption and consequently, vehicle-related CO₂ emissions during operation. “Every tire contributes to the efficiency and operating costs of a truck and trailer combination. While attention often focuses on the steer and drive axles, trailer tires also play an important role in rolling resistance and fuel consumption,” says Hinnerk Kaiser, responsible for the development of truck and bus tires in the EMEA region at Continental. “With the Conti Eco HT 5, we are extending the benefits of our fifth-generation Conti Eco portfolio to the trailer axle and helping fleets improve the efficiency of their transport operations.”

A trailer typically runs on multiple tires that are continuously in contact with the road. As a result, trailer tires have a direct impact on stability, fuel efficiency and overall operating performance. Depending on vehicle configuration, trailer tires can account for up to 50 percent of the total rolling resistance of a truck and trailer combination*. The new Conti Eco HT 5 has been engineered to deliver a good balance of low rolling resistance and high mileage, while promoting even wear and providing reliable grip across a wide range of operating conditions. The tire incorporates rolling-resistance-optimized materials, a newly designed sidewall and advanced filler compounds to improve fuel efficiency.

An innovative tread compound and refined curing process contribute to high mileage and long service life, while a redesigned five-rib tread pattern promotes even wear, stable handling and consistent performance in varying weather and road conditions on both regional and long-haul routes. Compared with the Conti Hybrid HT3+, the new Conti Eco HT 5 delivers up to a 12 percent reduction in rolling resistance under specified test conditions**. These improvements can help fleets reduce fuel consumption, lower CO₂ emissions and decrease tire-related operating costs. “For the Conti Eco HT 5, our focus was on improving efficiency while maintaining durability,” explains Kaiser. “The combination of low rolling resistance, long service life and balanced wear characteristics can help fleets reduce tire-related operating costs while maintaining reliable performance in demanding transport operations.”

The Conti Eco Generation 5 portfolio forms part of Continental's broader effort to support customers in improving transport efficiency through technological innovation and optimized tire performance. By combining low rolling resistance, high mileage and long service life across all axle positions, the portfolio supports customers in addressing key industry challenges, including rising fuel costs, increasing regulatory and customer requirements related to transport efficiency and emissions reduction.

A Complete Solution for Freight Transport

The fifth-generation Conti Eco portfolio brings together steer, drive and trailer axle tires in a coordinated solution for freight transport. Combining low rolling resistance, high mileage and long service life, it helps fleet operators improve efficiency across the entire vehicle combination while supporting lower operating costs and reliable performance.

The Conti Eco HT 5 will be available starting September 2026 in the following sizes: 385/65 R 22.5 and 385/55 R 22.5.

* 2-Axle Tractor and 3-Axle Trailer combination fully loaded. ** Compared with the Conti Hybrid HT3+ predecessor product under specified test conditions. Test methodology, reference product and test conditions available on request.
